As both account for a major part of the organisation's overall energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green design and a number of energy-saving measures, including in-rack air conditioning systems, LED lighting equipment, and round-the-clock monitoring of power efficiency. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of the aforementioned data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to enhance overall energy efficiency. It has also begun preparing to obtain green data centre certification. The HKMA understands the importance of building a culture of sustainability, and therefore regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage staff to develop habits conducive to sustainability and to adopt green and digital ways of working. The HKMA shares green living tips with staff, as well as annual office-wide energy and paper consumption statistics, to remind them to help address environmental issues at the individual level; it also encourages staff to put forward suggestions on sustainability matters. Led by senior managers of the Administration Division, a focus group brings together staff from different departments to brainstorm and put forward ideas and concrete measures to promote a green working environment. Members of the focus group also serve as ambassadors when new green measures are introduced. The HKMA encourages the wider community to adopt more environmentally friendly practices and has launched a number of measures to enhance the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry and the economy as a whole, minimising the consumption of resources. The HKMA's "Submission Through Electronic Transmission" system (STET) is a one-stop platform that allows banks to submit documents to the HKMA electronically, covering various types of periodic returns required to be submitted weekly, monthly, quarterly or annually. Another system, "e-Delivery", is a secure electronic communication channel that allows the HKMA to issue information such as circulars and guidelines to banks. Both systems help save a large amount of paper each year. In handling bank complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken measures to support paperless submission of documents, and bank customers can lodge complaints through electronic channels and by completing online forms. The HKMA is also developing a new-generation management information system to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper records to digital records. To reduce paper use, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with its participants, including issuing circulars, account-opening and account-termination letters, and replying to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, CMU will continue to explore more green measures, including the adoption of automated electronic processes for internal communications and communications with external parties. The HKMA encourages the public to make greater use of electronic payment methods in place of cash and physical cheques by promoting the use of the faster payment systems (FPS) and stored value facilities. Further information on FPS and stored value facilities is set out in the chapter "Hong Kong as an International Financial Centre" in the HKMA Annual Report 2022. Distributing electronic lai see is simple and convenient, and can reduce the use of physical lai see packets and banknotes, thereby helping to promote sustainable development in Hong Kong. To this end, the HKMA continued to actively promote across various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to distribute electronic lai see during the Lunar New Year via online or mobile banking services using FPS or other e-wallet services. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organised various activities to attract users to use electronic lai see, such as providing festive user interfaces, enhancing functions to make usage more convenient, and launching lucky draws or cash rebates. The HKMA promotes electronic lai see on social media platforms For members of the public who choose to distribute physical lai see during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continued to encourage them to use "good-as-new banknotes", that is, used but still fresh banknotes, for packing lai see. Good-as-new banknotes can reduce the need to print new banknotes, thereby reducing environmental impact. Feedback from the note-issuing banks indicates that the public has become increasingly accepting of good-as-new banknotes in recent years. The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA's efforts to promote coin recycling. Coins collected through the programme are recirculated into the market to meet public demand, improving the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need for minting. The programme operates two Coin Carts, which have to date served over one million people and collected more than 800 million coins with a total face value of about HKD 1.3 billion. In 2022, about 78% of users chose to use part or all of their coin value to top up their stored value facility accounts. The HKMA has maintained ongoing cooperation with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying Coin Carts to collect coins on non-governmental organisations' flag days, in a dedicated effort to support social services. The coin-counting machine on the Coin Cart The Coin Collection Programme was launched in 2014 and was the world's first systematic coin collection programme to adopt the mobile-vehicle concept. Over the years, it has won numerous local and international awards, with its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin handling widely recognised. The programme operates two Coin Carts, each equipped with two high-speed coin-counting machines to collect coins exchanged by the public. Members of the public can choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, use them to top up their stored value facility accounts (such as Octopus cards or e-wallets), or donate them to the Community Chest as charitable contributions. In addition to collecting coins, the Coin Carts are also assigned from time to time for various educational activities (such as student visits).

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the climate targets ("Climate Targets") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Climate Targets were established with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual ("SBTi Corporate Manual"). The purpose of this verification exercise was to verify whether the Climate Targets were established with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. This verification exercise was carried out in accordance with the "International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) – Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form opinions and conclusions so as to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the data. Our verification work is fully independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and concludes: • The Climate Targets were established with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Shum Siu-yan, Lead Auditor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023. Verification Statement: The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the 2022 environmental data ("2022 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2022 Data include the total energy consumption for 2022, the Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions intensity, the paper consumption intensity, and the intensity and recycling rate of non-hazardous waste generated, as well as the changes in these data relative to 2015 levels. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly issued by the World Resources Institute ("WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development ("WBCSD"). The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, and also covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for comparison of annual performance. The scope of verification comprised a total of 6 office and warehouse assets: 4 offices at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre; and 2 warehouses at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre and 6) Sung Lee Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan respectively. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification exercise was carried out in accordance with the "International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) – Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form opinions and conclusions so as to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and presentation of the data. Our verification work is fully independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the process of preparing the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2022 Data and concludes: • The 2022 Data are substantially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shum Siu-yan, Lead Auditor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023.

Scaling up and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing issue of our time. Almost half of the critical decade for the climate crisis has now passed. We need to cut global carbon emissions by more than 40% within this decade if we are to have any hope of limiting global warming to within 1.5 degrees Celsius. Yet greenhouse gas emissions keep reaching record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window to limit the global temperature rise to within 1.5 degrees Celsius will soon close. Everyone can clearly feel the impact of the 1.1 degree Celsius temperature rise—record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding and storms, and other extreme weather events are occurring more frequently across the globe, each more severe than the last. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, after being battered by a fierce super typhoon, we were immediately hit by a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Although we have good infrastructure and can respond swiftly to disasters, the impact was still very severe—widespread flooding, traffic disruptions, and damage to roads in numerous locations. All of these serve as a clear reminder that decisive and proactive climate action is truly a matter of urgency. Asia faces particularly significant challenges on the road to a low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means an easy task. Owing to the region's rapid economic development and fast-growing population, its carbon emissions account for more than half of the global total. At the same time, the Asia Pacific region is densely populated and, given its geographical location, is also susceptible to rising sea levels and extreme weather. As the economies in the region are at different stages of development, the low-carbon transition may bring new opportunities to some economies, but for others, raising the necessary transition financing poses an enormous challenge. The market estimates that the Asia Pacific region will require more than US$3 trillion in low-carbon transition investment annually over the next 30 years. As one of the world's international financial centres, Hong Kong has both the capacity and the responsibility to harness the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across the entire Asian region. As the regulator of the banking sector, a market facilitator, and a responsible investor, the HKMA has consistently devoted significant efforts to the sustainability agenda. Readers will learn from the various chapters of this report about the specific measures and work the HKMA has introduced over the past year. In addition, to strengthen the HKMA's internal governance structure and to more effectively coordinate sustainability work across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee last year. For details on this Steering Committee, please refer to the newly added chapter "Governance for Sustainability". Hong Kong's banks play an important role in supporting Asia's transition to net-zero emissions. In addition to fulfilling the traditional functions of a banking sector regulator by ensuring that banks properly manage climate risk in our day-to-day supervisory work, we also play the role of a facilitator, supporting the banking sector in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green classification framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype of the green classification framework for consultation in May and are now refining the framework based on the feedback collected during the consultation period. In addition, as there is a growing need across all sectors for higher-quality and more globally comparable sustainability disclosure information, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards launched by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June, namely a comprehensive global baseline of sustainability reporting. The HKMA's role as a facilitator is not limited to developing frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing the pain points faced by the industry. Currently, many banks are constrained by data limitations, making it difficult to conduct physical risk assessments. In light of this, the HKMA will soon launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform, whereby banks can simply enter a property address to assess the impact of physical hazards on Hong Kong's residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios, thereby helping banks manage the relevant climate risk. As one of Asia's leading international financial centres and a sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has long served as a bridge, channelling international investment into sustainable development projects in Asia and supporting the region's low-carbon transition. In recent years, the total amount of international green and sustainable bonds arranged for issuance in Hong Kong has accounted for over one-third of the Asian market, clearly leading other regions. It is particularly worth mentioning that the Shenzhen Municipal Government and the Hainan Provincial Government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong in 2023 for the third and second consecutive year respectively, once again affirming Hong Kong's important role as the green gateway connecting the Mainland with the rest of the world. The flourishing of Hong Kong's sustainable bond activity is partly attributable to the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling approximately US$25 billion to institutional and retail investors. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance in 2022 of the world's largest government retail green bonds, we issued the world's first batch of tokenised government green bond in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the issuance of a second batch of tokenised green bond; denominated in four major currencies and issued in digitally native form, this was the world's first multi-currency digital green bond. At the same time, we have proactively rolled out various measures to enhance the vibrancy and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. This covers work across multiple areas including skills training, improving data, green fintech, and transition finance. In particular, in terms of talent training, we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for banking in 2023, providing banking practitioners with systematic courses to enhance their understanding of and expertise in green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key area of our work; it provides funding for the decarbonisation activities of high-carbon-emitting and hard-to-abate industries, preventing these industries from being unable to transition due to a lack of financial support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong's green classification framework to cover transition activities. We will also expand the coverage of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, which provides funding to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, in order to encourage enterprises in the region to raise transition financing in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen our communication and engagement with relevant stakeholders, and through public-private cooperation and blended finance models, attract private-sector investment into sustainable development projects that have previously been more difficult to finance. Some of the above work requires cross-sectoral collaboration and is coordinated primarily by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, which is co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-standing collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office also joined the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment and the Partnership for Green Development and Investment and Financing as a founding member in 2023. In addition, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero also announced plans to establish a branch in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we hope to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, and in turn support the channelling of funds into sustainable development projects across the region and around the world. To drive new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped host the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week earlier this year, which attracted over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including top decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, to discuss solutions for scaling up climate financing in the region and to forge new partnerships in this regard. Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue delivered a speech at the "Asia Pacific Climate Business Forum", a flagship event of Hong Kong Green Week. As the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a globally significant asset owner, the HKMA leads by example in being a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been at the forefront of green and sustainable asset investment, and has progressively expanded the Exchange Fund's ESG and green asset holdings in both public and private markets. In respect of the goal of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's Investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA last year added an active global equity portfolio themed on sustainability and climate transition, while also expanding the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another public-market asset portfolio. In addition, the green, social, and sustainability bonds prioritised by the HKMA for investment have outperformed the investment benchmark, embodying the proposition of "doing well by doing good". In the private markets, we continued to pursue green-related investment opportunities and became an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. At the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio was reduced by 6% and 46% compared with the 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and has consistently remained below the overall market level. As a sustainability-oriented institution, the HKMA will continue to strive for improvement, setting our sustainability goals and plans on the basis of the three pillars of environmental, staff, and social responsibility. Specifically, on its low-carbon transition journey, the HKMA continuously strengthens its capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emissions reduction, improving energy efficiency, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of achieving our commitment to net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have formulated plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the short term, and have made good progress towards our interim target of Scope 2 emissions reduction by 2030. To attract and retain outstanding talent to fulfil the HKMA's important functions, in addition to our green goals, the HKMA is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of our staff. Furthermore, by working with various stakeholders, we promote financial inclusion, enhance the public's level of financial literacy, and raise public awareness of guarding against financial fraud, thereby contributing to the creation of a caring society. The climate challenge is enormous and exceptionally urgent. Economies around the world are moving towards a more sustainable future, a process that is expected to bring about tremendous changes in financing activities and asset allocation. This transition carries considerable risks, but will also be accompanied by unprecedented opportunities. As one of the world's leading sustainable finance hubs, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in action to address these challenges. At the same time, we are also well-positioned to seize the momentum. The HKMA will fully support the industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition; and will continue to lead by example as a responsible investor and a sustainable institution, working with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda of our time. Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are of global concern. In its sustainability work, the HKMA aims to demonstrate leadership through its own policies and operations, to ensure that Hong Kong's financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to climate change risks, and to support the transition to more sustainable economic development. Through active participation in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also strive to contribute to the formulation of regional and global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As the banking sector regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking sector's climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, the priority tasks include: launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting a new round of consultation meetings, as part of the review of banks' progress in implementing the supervisory requirements on climate risk management; continuing the work on incorporating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; completing the second round of the industry-wide climate risk stress-tested exercise, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing the observations and lessons learnt with the industry; enhancing sustainability disclosures, including working with relevant local authorities to keep the relevant requirements aligned with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards as a global baseline, and making preparations for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Pillar 3 framework on climate-related financial risks; and sharing with the industry guidance on best practices in transition planning. To promote the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to keep abreast of local and international market and regulatory developments, and stay in touch with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate selling processes. In addition, the HKMA will also play a facilitator role, striving to promote the development of the green finance ecosystem and to support banks in providing financing for economic transition. We will soon publish a local green taxonomy and continue to expand its coverage to encompass more activities such as transition activities. At the same time, we will also continue to explore the application of technology solutions to assist banks in identifying, measuring and monitoring their climate risk exposures; one example is the soon-to-be-launched cloud-based platform, which will facilitate banks' physical risk assessments. To enhance the professional competencies of practitioners, in 2024 we will also develop the professional level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners. Hong Kong is well-placed and has distinct advantages to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the proposals in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope covered by the Government Green Bond Programme to sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bonds market; at the same time, through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, attracting more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions and enterprises to raise green funds through Hong Kong, and explore the potential synergies between green finance and technology. In addition, we will continue to assist in implementing the Government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. As co-chair of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and work in promoting the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Group will focus on three areas of work, including sustainability disclosures, the application of technology and transition finance. As another priority area of work, through the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various dedicated initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing insightful market analysis, offering targeted professional training for banks, and providing practical guidance to help banks support financial institutions in establishing their tailored green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our cooperation with the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero, the Coalition for Climate Resilient Investment, and the Green Investment and Financing Partnership. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving the goal of net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's Investment Portfolio by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to strengthen the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring the resilience of the asset portfolio on the path towards net zero. We fully understand that achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement requires an economy-wide transition, and therefore we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus, while balancing the Exchange Fund's investment objectives, on assets that can bring positive climate benefits to the real economy. As an environmentally responsible institution, the HKMA's decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest developments in the market, regulation, technology and other climate-related areas. To further strengthen the HKMA's climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage staff to participate in our sustainability work, including launching campaigns to cultivate sustainable habits and optimising office processes and practices. Moreover, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices when selecting and renewing contracts. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the designated certification standards. In terms of the regular upgrading of data centre facilities, in addition to keeping abreast of the latest technological developments, we will also integrate green design and practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and consolidation, and actively modernise internal systems to enhance efficiency and minimise potential risks as much as possible. Finally, in the area of social focus, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues, and work with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, as well as raise public awareness of guarding against financial fraud.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its related impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, a banking sector regulator, a market facilitator, a responsible investor and a sustainable development institution, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. To fulfil its commitment to good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework for sustainability-related work, with clear accountability arrangements and a high level of transparency. This framework leads the formulation of the HKMA's relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of related measures, and ensures that sustainability factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and working practices. It ensures that sustainability factors are effectively incorporated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the progress and effectiveness of sustainability work. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which are responsible for monitoring the HKMA's work, including its work on sustainability, and making recommendations; the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; in the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and for other functional areas, the relevant teams and working groups responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), jointly initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion of the scope of the HKMA's various sustainability initiatives over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a brand-new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas.¹ It provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of the banking sector, market development, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; assesses the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG targets; and oversees external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. In addition, we invite the Assistant Chief Executives responsible for the key functions related to green and sustainability matters to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on the key achievements of their work and future plans. The Steering Committee holds regular meetings and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Departments, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC jointly initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020.² As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates the cross-sectoral work on the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, in order to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally among the world's financial centres. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Building of a Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals as well as the global sustainable development agenda. Banks encounter the impacts of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their day-to-day business operations. To continue to perform their vital functions within the financial system and channel more funds towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risk. As the regulator of the banking sector, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capabilities to respond to and manage climate risk, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The HKMA is dedicated to formulating various policy measures to strengthen the banking system's ability to respond to climate risk. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to help banks maintain safety and soundness in the course of the economy's transition to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of the circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey of selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices on transition planning with the industry, and will hold seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experiences within the industry. On the disclosure front, in response to the latest international developments, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards published in June and the consultation launched by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) in November on the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks, the HKMA is stepping up its work to enhance the sustainability-related disclosure framework of Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is working with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that aligns with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA enhanced its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to banks to help them further improve their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process. Climate risk management is now a standing item on the agenda of prudential supervisory meetings held with banks' management. Banking supervisors have also adopted the enhanced CAMEL rating system¹, which has incorporated climate risk factors, to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, the HKMA revised the "green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, in order to encourage banks to enhance their risk management frameworks in response to climate risk. Key work priorities under the two-year plan in 2023 Following the conclusion of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual, the HKMA launched a round of thematic examinations on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. The thematic examination covered four major areas, including the governance framework for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and institutional culture, awareness and communication. The HKMA made a number of enhancements to the climate risk stress testing framework, including introducing a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of the simultaneous occurrence of economic and climate change shocks. Following these enhancements, and as part of the HKMA's regular supervisor-led stress testing exercises, a second round of climate risk stress testing was launched in June to comprehensively assess banks' climate risk exposures and to further enhance banks' capabilities in managing climate risk. A total of 44 banks participated in this round of stress testing, an increase of more than 60% compared with the first pilot scheme in 2021. The HKMA also held a climate risk stress testing forum in November, which was attended by as many as 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating the sharing of experiences among banks, this event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk quantification. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks' progress in implementing module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual. The HKMA held meetings with banks' management to discuss their work on climate risk management and the common challenges facing the industry, and reviewed the information provided by banks and other publicly available information to assess their progress. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue enhancing their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's supervisory expectations. As global attention to climate change grows and efforts to address the issue intensify, the HKMA has observed increasing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering such products to meet customer needs. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks' sale of green and sustainable investment products and issued a circular in November setting out the standards the HKMA expects banks to meet and sharing observed good practices. This circular covers multiple areas including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training and record-keeping, and aims to mitigate potential greenwashing risks and enhance investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of the relevant investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can enhance data availability and risk analysis, strengthening banks' capabilities in managing climate risk. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot version of a cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technology solutions can assist in conducting physical risk assessments. On another front, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) approaches through the application of advanced analytics and A.I., in order to reduce the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby enhancing banks' processes for submitting AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the HKMA organised the "Green Fintech Competition", which aimed to seek market-ready solutions to help the banking sector address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted a total of more than 85 entries from around 70 companies. In December, the HKMA held the "Green and Sustainable Banking Conference", providing a platform for the banking sector and the technology community to explore the role of low-carbon technology and green fintech in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and the Mainland, and announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition" at the same event. This event attracted around 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulators and academia. To enhance transparency in financial markets and to bring greater consistency to green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA developed a local green classification framework with the assistance of a consultancy firm. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Prototype of the Hong Kong Green Classification Framework", seeking stakeholders' views on the establishment and implementation of a green classification catalogue. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying other areas for the next phase of the framework's development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force, which has identified environmental crimes as predicate offences for money laundering; and given the interconnection between AML and environmental, social and governance (ESG), this area is receiving increasing attention from regulators. The HKMA is keenly aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing monitoring efforts. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its continuous monitoring of financial stability risks, and incorporates analysis of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps to further enrich climate scenarios, giving central banks and regulators a clearer understanding of the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the transition planning workstream under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participates in analysing the interactions between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to develop a forward-looking and dynamic perspective in examining climate-related financial risks. On the research front, the HKMA has conducted a number of applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial industry and the economy. Research topics include the climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds², ESG fund flows³, the impact of climate change on housing prices⁴, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance in the global supply chain⁵. The above research findings enhance the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, and help inform the formulation of relevant policies. On the local front, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risk on financial stability. On the external front, the HKMA also shares its research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through international events on climate-related matters and various channels such as the HKMA Research Memorandum. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a collateralised standby liquidity facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. In line with the NGFS's recommendations, the HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on responding to climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, the HKMA helps to promote international and regional policy dialogue on responding to climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws on the insights gained to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to jointly build a richer ecosystem and promote the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategy. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to support Hong Kong in seizing sustainable finance opportunities, with major areas of work including sustainability disclosure, strengthening ecosystem building, transition finance and green fintech. Specifically, a Working Group on Sustainability Disclosure has been established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will cover 4 key areas, including sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Working Group on Transition Finance has also been established to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group is also strengthening the building of a sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. In particular, on the data front, we continued to promote the adoption of the climate and environmental risk questionnaire for non-listed corporates that the Steering Group launched in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region and globally. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced 3 new key initiatives to seize the investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia Pacific region. To facilitate the industry's skills training, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the Government's "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Training Scheme", which provides subsidies to practitioners, students and graduates who receive green and sustainable finance-related training and attain relevant qualifications. As at December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications had been registered as eligible training or qualifications under the Scheme, and over 560 subsidy applications had been approved. The HKMA also launched the foundation level of the new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners". This module aims to promote talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional competency of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking sector to develop the professional level of this module, in order to meet the industry's rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals. To help financial institutions and corporates, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, better understand key climate and sustainability-related topics, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and transition planning, during the year the HKMA, together with relevant Government policy bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), organised a series of seminars and thematic workshops, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. On the student front, following the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Initiative" in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to deepen the understanding of sustainable finance among interns and university undergraduate degree programme graduates. The HKMA is well aware of the potential of technology to fill climate-related data gaps and improve data quality, and is therefore committed to making relevant data more accessible and improving data quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancement measures to provide a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information for financial institutions, corporates and the public. Key enhancements include an e-platform for sustainability disclosure, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralised data and resources that are easier to browse and search. During "Hong Kong Green Week", the Steering Group also co-organised the "Harnessing Technology to Catalyse Sustainable Finance" event with Cyberport and Invest Hong Kong, showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week — Finance Theme" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted over 1,600 guests from close to 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia and consultancy firms. The highlight of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the "Asia Pacific Climate Business Forum" co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together over 400 guests, including top decision-makers in the global business and financial sectors, to discuss solutions to unlock climate financing in the Asia Pacific region. This two-day event covered a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industries, circular economy, the future development of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in emerging and developing markets in the Asia Pacific region. The forum received responses from public and private sector institutions, which co-organised over 10 roundtables, seminars and other exchange activities. The topics covered climate financing, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomy and green development financing in Belt and Road regions. In addition, the HKMA co-organised the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" with the International Monetary Fund on 29 February 2024, to explore key measures to scale up climate financing, as well as the role of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. The above activities are part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, and can serve as a useful platform to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address the climate financing challenges in the Asia Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks", as a collaboration platform bringing together financial institutions, banking industry organisations, research institutions and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held a total of 22 training events and roundtables, attracting over 7,300 participants from around the world, including the Asia Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, together with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second research report on a cutting-edge topic, entitled "Developing an Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategy: Case Studies". During the year, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established "Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment" (CASI) and the "Green Investment and Finance Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Initiative Green Development International Alliance. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will help facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more funds into green and sustainable projects in Asia and the wider region. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of a Hong Kong chapter, which helps support the net-zero efforts of local and Mainland financial institutions. The HKMA assists GFANZ's work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. The HKMA assists in the issuance of green bonds under the Programme. To date, the Government has issued green institutional and retail bonds equivalent to approximately US$25 billion, with the proceeds raised allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Programme, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report", detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. In the 2023-24 financial year, the Government continued its regular green institutional bond issuance and issued green bonds equivalent to approximately US$6 billion in June. This tri-currency issuance covered bonds of various tenors in US dollar, euro and renminbi, attracting different types of investors, with an enthusiastic subscription response recording subscription amounts of close to US$30 billion equivalent. Among them, the issuance size of the renminbi bonds was increased from RMB10 billion issued in January to RMB15 billion, with a 10-year renminbi bond introduced for the first time, which helps extend the Government's renminbi yield curve and further enrich the range of CNH product offerings. The enthusiastic response of global investors to the Government's green bond issuance reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued the second batch of green Retail Bonds with a total value of HKD20 billion, further promoting market development and advancing financial inclusion. This issuance provided the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, allowing them to both participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a key role in advancing the development of green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has been leading the way in green and sustainable asset investment, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership and to integrate environmental, social and governance factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term value creation",¹ believing that giving full consideration to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate relevant investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and to set a "2050 net-zero emissions" target for its portfolio,² the HKMA is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasising sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and pursuing more desirable long-term risk-adjusted returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry practice standards, and promoting the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and central banks. Through stewardship and collaborative measures, the HKMA is committed to fostering a future in which finance and sustainable development go hand in hand.  **Chart 1 — The Exchange Fund's responsible investment journey.**  Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is essential for integrating sustainability and for planning a credible climate transition to achieve net-zero targets. To fulfil its commitment to support the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) Glasgow Declaration³ and the strategic plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA leads by example by preparing this chapter on the responsible investment of the Exchange Fund in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The foremost guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to balance the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund while practising responsible investment. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors relevant implementation through regular meeting reports from the sustainable investment team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Chart 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategist, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions and progress of work discussed at the quarterly meetings of the ESG Committee are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Strategist of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets semi-annually to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures of the HKMA's various functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives.  **Chart 2 — The responsible investment governance structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office.**  As shown in Chart 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, with an initial focus on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainable development evolved rapidly and, beyond risk considerations, became a priority strategic focus of major institutions around the world, the Exchange Fund Investment Office revisited its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone, when the Exchange Fund Investment Office established a new business strategy division led by the Chief Strategist, responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, and incorporating the responsible investment dedicated team—now known as the sustainable investment team—which was originally under the Risk Management and Compliance Department. This strategic reorganisation reflects the HKMA's elevation of the focus of responsible investment from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainable development-related matters in investment. The sustainable investment team works closely with various teams of the Exchange Fund Investment Office on the integration of ESG factors, and assists senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the ESG—especially climate-related—risks and opportunities of various investments: Public market investments—The Credit, Rules and Compliance Committee, comprising senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the views of the sustainable investment team, and monitors the ESG status of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reporting from the Risk Management and Compliance Department. In addition, the sustainable investment team also participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring process of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see the section "Promoting active exercise of asset ownership" under the "Risk Management" section on page 40). Private market investments—The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal. The HKMA understands that the physical and transition risks⁴ posed by climate change, as well as the related opportunities, will affect the long-term performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investments. The Emissions Gap Report 2023⁵ published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that unless countries around the world make further cuts to greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels before 2030. The pressing need for more aggressive policies, technological development or behavioural change to keep temperature rises in check may intensify transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded asset shocks. At the same time, extreme weather events are becoming increasingly frequent and severe, posing additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future is aligned with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the Exchange Fund's portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The following sections elaborate on the relevant approaches.  **Chart 3 — The HKMA's three-pronged approach in responsible investment.**  In progressing towards its net-zero target, the HKMA tends to proactively engage in dialogue rather than exclude or divest from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is critical to achieving the primary investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe and have a potential impact on investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess outstanding technology and good corporate governance to respond to evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not help resolve the issue of carbon emissions. On the contrary, the HKMA supports these industries through deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, driving them to implement transitions to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about favourable change for themselves and for the world at large. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategies, taking a comprehensive approach to pursue transition outcomes aligned with the Exchange Fund's and global net-zero targets, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to facilitate the climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio (Chart 4). The HKMA's responsible investment maintained good momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new actively managed global equity portfolio themed on sustainability and climate transition, managed by external investment managers, and expanded the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another portfolio managed by external investment managers. In addition, the green, social responsibility and sustainability bonds that the HKMA prioritised for investment outperformed the investment benchmark, demonstrating the philosophy of "doing well by doing good". In private markets, the HKMA actively built a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic development trends such as the climate and energy transition. For example, during the year the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, reflecting the HKMA's dedication to addressing Asia's climate transition needs.  **Chart 4 — Ongoing measures to promote ESG investment.**  The HKMA has invested in a company that specialises in producing environmentally friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste (including organic matter such as food waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on energy-intensive high-temperature environments to produce plastics, this company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This plastic material, produced 100% from waste, can serve as an alternative to the oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and durable consumer goods, offering a sustainable and versatile option. At the same time, this plastic material is also compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is a firm supporter of the circular economy.
