The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organisation, adopting a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also attaches importance to the physical and mental well-being of its staff and to social responsibility, and strives to promote financial inclusion as well as to enhance the financial literacy of the public. As a responsible organisation, the HKMA has set sustainability targets under the three pillars of environment, staff and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (the Steering Committee),1 established in October and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for various organisational sustainability initiatives. The Steering Committee's predecessor was the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategy and policies on organisational sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and regularly submits progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Focus Group and the Volunteer Service Team provide support for coordinating the organisation's sustainability work; the former serves as a platform for pooling ideas and brainstorming on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of participating in volunteer activities. The HKMA has drawn up a roadmap to guide its transition path. The focus of the work is to implement carbon reduction strategies in its daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green mobility, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools and more environmentally friendly modes of operation, reducing waste, and building a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to apply internal carbon pricing tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and to adopt carbon offset measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce more environmentally friendly operational solutions for the wider community, covering channels applicable to banks for submitting electronic documents and communications, as well as electronic payment and coin collection schemes for use by the general public. To strengthen and maintain its operational capabilities, the HKMA employs a professional team, builds a talent pool, and attaches importance to the physical and mental well-being of its staff. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages staff to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers the use of social enterprises (SEs) in procurement; promotes consumer education on financial services; and works with the banking sector to ensure that all sectors of society can have fair access to basic banking services. The remainder of this chapter sets out the details of the above strategies. Under the HKMA's overall organisational risk management framework, the Risk Committee,2 chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats that the HKMA faces in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts brought about by climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by more extreme weather, could affect the HKMA's offices and hinder staff commuting. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plans to cope with extreme weather situations. The HKMA also regularly conducts evacuation and back-up facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. A number of measures have also been incorporated into the design of the offices to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy use, air travel and waste disposal. The HKMA has been monitoring the transition risks it bears by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 (air travel) in all areas of its organisational operations by 2050 or earlier. As a near-term emission reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing vehicles to electric vehicles; and, using 2015 as the base year, to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various carbon reduction and offset strategies. Despite the challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will nonetheless adopt a multi-pronged approach within what is practicable to minimise Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions (such as paper consumption, waste generation and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were formulated with reference to the "Science Based Targets initiative" methodology, which has also been validated by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emissions, energy and paper consumption, and waste data disclosed in this report.6 The scope and basis of the verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the Annual Report 2022, the HKMA also independently published the Sustainability Report 2022 for the first time. The HKMA's efforts to strengthen ESG reporting were recognised, with the HKMA receiving the ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulator to receive an award in this category. The panel of judges praised the HKMA for meeting good ESG standards, noting that the Sustainability Report is clear and easy to read, and that the appointment of an independent organisation to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflects its commitment to reporting with high transparency and accountability. In addition, the HKMA also received the highest rating, the Gold Award in the "Non-Profit-Making and Charitable Organisations" category, in the Hong Kong Management Association's "Best Annual Reports Awards 2023". The panel of judges praised the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making good use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's determination to enhance financial literacy and promote financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its staff and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impacts arising from its operations, and its internal "Green Office Guidelines" provide staff with guidance on the use of resources and the generation of office waste. The HKMA has incorporated environmental factors into the design, operation and maintenance of the offices it owns and leases. When renovating offices, existing furniture and renovation materials are reused as far as possible to reduce waste, and environmentally friendly construction and decoration materials are given priority. The HKMA has consistently adopted this practice, and as a result, in 2021 and 2022 respectively, some of its offices that had completed renovation at Two International Finance Centre were awarded Gold-level certification under LEED7 and the "BEAM Plus Interiors" assessment.8 Enhancing energy efficiency by adopting new technologies and making good use of existing ones remains one of the HKMA's key areas of focus. In addition to promoting good habits, such as switching off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include the use of light-emitting diode lighting equipment, motion sensors, setting air-conditioning room temperatures at appropriate levels, and making good use of energy in the information technology network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has continued to decrease, standing at 2.59 megawatt-hours per person in 2023,9 a decline of 29.7% from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions mainly come from the greenhouse gas emissions arising from the consumption of electricity generated by fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO2e per person,10 a decrease of 45.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software and meeting facilities, the HKMA has also adopted digital tools and technologies, automated and streamlined workflows, and built a digital working environment, strengthening online collaboration within the organisation.11 Paperless meetings have become the HKMA's main mode of meeting. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, various internal administrative matters are mainly handled through electronic processes. In addition, the HKMA encourages staff to embrace green and digital working modes, using digital means in place of paper-based documents and communications. At the same time, work on implementing an electronic records-keeping system is also underway. The above green and digital measures have brought positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kilograms per person, a significant decrease of 64.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). As most international events have returned to being held in physical format following the COVID-19 pandemic, and there is also a need to promote the development of Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, it has been unavoidable for the relevant HKMA staff to travel overseas on business. To reduce the carbon emissions arising from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to take direct flights where feasible or to combine different business trips together when participating in overseas events. At the organisational level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO2e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA also participates in a "Gold Standard"12 certified carbon offset scheme to offset the remaining carbon emissions arising from air travel; the scheme carries out waste-to-energy conversion, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue with similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement process takes into account sustainability and environmental factors. As part of a comprehensive review of the organisation's procurement policies and procedures, the existing practice of procuring green products has been formalised into a formal system and complies with the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. In addition, the tender assessment criteria have also incorporated ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency. At the same time, all suppliers are required to undertake to comply with environmental regulations. In accordance with the "4R" principles, namely Refuse, Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimise waste generation and manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The breakdown of non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, is set out in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA directly participated for the first time in the red packet recycling scheme of the management company of the International Finance Centre office building. Staff handed in a total of about 3,000 used but still intact and pristine red packets. These red packets were subsequently handed over to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use in the following Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operational and back-up data centres account for a major part of the organisation's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE).13 In 2023, the HKMA's two data centres were awarded "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under the assessment guidelines "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres" issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organisation in Hong Kong to receive such ratings. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the 2023 environmental data ("2023 data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The 2023 data include the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste) for 2023, their respective intensities, and the changes in these data compared with the 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 data also include the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared with the level when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, and also covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (except for food waste). The scope of verification covers a total of five office and warehouse assets, of which four offices are located at 1) Two International Financial centres, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and the warehouse at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the five assets. This verification work was carried out in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusion in order to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data back to their source, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checking, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work was completely independent and impartial. The verification team of the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency was not involved in the preparation process of the 2023 data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 data and concludes that: the 2023 data are materially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024

The threats posed by climate change are imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record, and also the first year in which the global temperature exceeded pre-industrial levels by the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius. At the same time, although global greenhouse gas emissions moderated somewhat during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current measures to mitigate climate change. In the process of addressing global warming, the manifestation of climate-related risks is bound to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Moreover, current geopolitical tensions, an increasingly fragmented global economic landscape, potentially worsening energy security concerns, and an uncertain economic outlook all pose greater challenges for countries in tackling climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Across the globe, Asia in particular faces the most formidable transition challenges. As the World Economic Forum has pointed out, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth, but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a crucial role in whether the world can successfully achieve the goal of net-zero emissions. As a leading international financial centre in Asia, Hong Kong needs to strengthen its leading role and fully harness the power of finance to support and drive the region's transition. To this end, the HKMA last year published the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda", setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating the concept of sustainable development into the core of the financial system. On the one hand, our work focuses on enhancing the ability of the banking sector to address climate change-related risks, and on the other hand, it focuses on helping the industry seize the relevant new opportunities. At the same time, we also lead by example and play a guiding role. The HKMA's sustainable development work encompasses four major areas: supporting the banking sector in moving towards net-zero emissions, investing for a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and driving more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a crucial role in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and Asia, but in the process of transition it also faces considerable risks itself. In the "Action Agenda", we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030, and net-zero emissions in their financing by 2050. At the same time, we require all banks to enhance their disclosures of climate change-related risks and opportunities. While continuously strengthening banks' climate risk management, we also provide guidance for banks' transition planning to help them enhance their capacity to respond to the transition and better manage the relevant risks. We are also undertaking preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong's sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with a view to further enhancing the industry's transparency in the relevant activities. In addition, we are enhancing the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched in May last year to incorporate more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We hope that by providing clear criteria, we can guide more capital towards sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change brings significant physical and transition risks, which may affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investment projects. But at the same time, it also brings opportunities for the Exchange Fund to grow and drive positive impacts. Our experience has demonstrated that investment returns and positive sustainable impacts can be reconciled with each other, and there is no conflict between them. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in the Exchange Fund's "portfolio" by 2050, and have pledged in the "Action Agenda" to support Asia's climate transition through the Exchange Fund's investments. At present, sustainable investments already account for more than 10% of the "portfolio". To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships in November last year with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the International Finance Corporation, to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in Asia through co-investment. In addition, in September last year we published the first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise asset ownership and adopt good sustainable investment practices. The flow of funds is particularly important for accelerating the region's transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuance for Asian issuers (including mainland provincial and municipal governments), Hong Kong plays an important role in channelling capital to accelerate the region's transition. The "Action Agenda" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable financing platform, as well as the goal of promoting innovation in sustainable finance. From leveraging the demonstrative role of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to drive innovation in green bonds (including the issuance of the world's first batch of multi-currency digital bonds in February last year), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" in May last year to cover transition financing instruments, and to the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" launched in November last year, we have been committed to encouraging issuers in the region to use Hong Kong's financial platform to raise the funds needed for decarbonisation transition. To achieve a robust transition, in addition to capital and innovation, an inclusive and easily accessible sustainable development ecosystem is also needed for support. This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent information disclosure, as well as industry talent equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, in the "Action Agenda" we have committed to supporting the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosure, and to striving to bridge the gap in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosure, in particular by providing convenient and easy-to-use climate disclosure templates to facilitate the sustainability disclosure of small and medium-sized enterprises. In November last year, we also launched the "Green and Sustainable Finance" professional-level module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for banking practitioners, to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. In addition, through the first Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we have enabled people from all sectors to participate in discussions on sustainable development, thereby promoting collaboration and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with the vision of sustainable development. In the "Action Agenda", we have committed to achieving net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030, which is 20 years ahead of our original commitment. In addition, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap promulgated by the Government. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024, and have incorporated low carbon emissions as a screening factor in the procurement process. At the same time, we continue to improve work efficiency through digitalisation, foster a culture of sustainable development within the organisation, and motivate staff to actively participate in sustainable development work. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic shifts in geopolitics have added uncertainties to global climate action. However, climate change is an indisputable fact and is gradually intensifying. In our work to address climate change, the current situation does not allow us the slightest complacency. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risk on Hong Kong's financial system, while bringing us opportunities in the process. Entering 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, striving to advance our sustainable development work and deepen our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the formidable challenges ahead, we will, as always, remain committed to supporting Hong Kong, Asia and other regions in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is one of the defining challenges facing our generation. As international financial centres and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across Asia and the world. In October 2024, the HKMA published its "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), setting out the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timeline for achieving various goals, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance the relevant efforts. Through formulating strategic policies, strengthening supervisory engagement, and enhancing internal operations, the HKMA plans to reinforce the ability of Hong Kong's financial industry and the HKMA itself to address climate risk, and to promote the transition of Asia towards a more sustainable economy. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA is also committed to exerting its influence and taking part in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both the regional and global levels. As the banking sector regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector, and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness in the course of transitioning to net zero. Our priority tasks in 2025 include: - Launching a new round of thematic examinations on banks' climate risk management practices, and conducting a third round of consultation sessions to review banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant supervisory requirements, and to further strengthen banks' climate risk management capabilities; - Refining the incorporation of climate risk stress-tested into the HKMA's supervisor-driven stress-tested framework; - Continuing to advance the incorporation of climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; - Commencing preparatory work on formulating relevant supervisory requirements for the local banking sector's implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's forthcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks, as well as the International Financial Reporting Standards for Sustainability Disclosure (ISSB Standards); - Completing the preparation of a new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual, providing guidance to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing with the industry good practices on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to being the banking sector regulator, the HKMA also plays a facilitator role, committed to promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We have published the first phase of the "Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance", providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and to facilitate related funding. The HKMA has commenced work on the second phase of the taxonomy to expand its coverage, including adding transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate change adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will host another green fintech event in 2025 to promote banks' adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well positioned to support the sustainable financing needs in the region. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme", whose expanded coverage will include sustainable projects, such as social responsibility projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bonds market and set an example for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable funds. We will also step up our promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions and enterprises from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing subsidies to prospective issuers of digital green bond through the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme". While the demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures by institutions and enterprises is increasing, different entities vary in their capabilities and readiness to make sustainability disclosures, and some entities may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and more inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their customers with a richer set of climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how to leverage technology to further make existing resources more accessible and easier to use; and collaborate with major local industry organisations to provide the training the industry needs. The sustainable finance markets are rapidly evolving, requiring an expanded local talent pool and the bridging of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. The HKMA's key tasks in 2025 include collaborating with the banking sector to develop professional-level training courses for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Enhanced Competency Framework on Green and Sustainable Finance", and identifying areas where the industry has further training needs through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030" study. In addition, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the government-funded "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme", and to review the scope of the scheme. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks" to launch dedicated initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing insightful market analysis, offering targeted skills enhancement and training support, promoting community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in developing roadmaps to grow green finance into a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier, in support of the overall economic transition. Through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, we will continue to enhance the sustainability of the exchange Fund's investments, primarily focusing on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio, while exploring investment opportunities that can promote positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to leading by example in its institutional sustainability efforts. In line with the accelerated timeline for achieving the net-zero commitment announced in the "Action Agenda", the HKMA will progressively incorporate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment and reporting at a pragmatic pace, continuing to advance institutional sustainability. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on material topics. In addition, we will conduct an energy audit and use technology solutions to assess the significant impacts of climate risk on our offices and operations, so as to enhance our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government's published "Hong Kong Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure" and are actively undertaking preparatory work to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment, following the principles of energy efficiency and energy conservation, to select data centres for planned upgrade projects. We will also expand our digital measures to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and enhancing the overall digital experience of our staff, banks and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, a banking sector regulator, a market facilitator, a responsible investor and a sustainable development organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the Asian region. The HKMA has in place a robust sustainable development governance framework that leads the formulation of the HKMA's relevant strategies and policies; oversees the implementation of relevant measures; and ensures that sustainable development factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and working practices. In its commitment to good corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainable development governance framework for its sustainable development-related work, featuring clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency. This governance framework ensures that sustainable development factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainable development work. The HKMA's sustainable development governance framework comprises: - the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its related dedicated sub-committees, which are responsible for monitoring the HKMA's work, including its work on sustainable development, and for making recommendations; - the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA's Chief Executive, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; - in the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - for other functional areas, the relevant groups and working groups, which are responsible for planning and implementing sustainable development measures relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), jointly established by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's various sustainable development initiatives over the past years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainable development work across the HKMA's different functional areas. The Steering Committee is responsible for: - providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across four functional areas, namely the banking sector, the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; - overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; - assessing the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG targets; and - overseeing the external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the HKMA's Chief Executive, with the three Deputy Chief Executives as permanent members. In addition, we will invite the Assistant Chief Executives dedicated to key functions relating to green and sustainability matters to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on the key achievements of and future plans for their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's banking departments, the Corporate Development and Operations Department, the External Department and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainable development measures, the HKMA, together with the SFC, jointly initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts on the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, so as to consolidate Hong Kong's position as one of the leading green and sustainable finance centres in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system in coping with climate risk, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their day-to-day business operations, and must therefore proactively manage climate risk. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system by channelling funds towards green and sustainable projects. As the regulator of the banking sector, the HKMA is placing particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risk, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), setting out the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as one of the sustainable finance centres in the region and to support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The "Action Agenda" comprises eight major goals across four dimensions. To help the industry achieve the goals of the relevant banking policies, we have been carrying out the various initiatives set out below. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or before, and net-zero emissions in their financing by 2050 or before. All banks are to enhance the transparency of climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices in transition planning with the industry, and launched an industry consultation on the draft of the Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-2 "Transition Planning". The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to respond to the net-zero transition and on the related risk management. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating into the assessment process the relevant factors put forward by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (the Basel Committee) on the effective management of climate-related financial risks, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risk. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the "Action Agenda". In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (the Taxonomy) to address the industry's concerns about greenwashing and to help channel funds towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, and aims to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating relevant elements to reflect local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope covered by the Taxonomy, and are consulting a broad range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable funds. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management, and was committed to supporting banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to respond to climate change. The HKMA also completed all the work of incorporating climate risk into the banking supervisory process under the two-year plan formulated in 2022. To promote banks in strengthening their capacity to manage climate risk, the HKMA shared with the banking sector the good practices observed in thematic examinations and consultation meetings, which mainly include: - establishing a robust governance framework that clearly sets out the responsibilities of the board and senior management; - ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters, namely (1) promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) building a sound climate risk culture within the organisation. In August, the HKMA held a Balanced Supervisory Roundtable on the theme of climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives exchanged views with HKMA participants on a number of climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress-tested, transition planning and finance. This roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and helped inform the HKMA's work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA launched a round of thematic examinations of banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, and assessed their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in the Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The thematic examinations covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress-tested. The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing the Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest supervisory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance based on the specific circumstances of each bank to support their climate risk management efforts. In 2024, the HKMA completed the second round of the banking sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST), with a total of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups participating. The results showed that, under various scenarios (including a hypothetical simultaneous occurrence of climate risk and a macroeconomic downturn), the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience in withstanding severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risk. A report setting out the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. The HKMA understands that banks encounter numerous challenges relating to data and methodology in climate risk management, and has therefore been committed to a range of initiatives to promote the application of technology in addressing these challenges. To address the problem of a lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for conducting climate risk assessments, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform in light of user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA collaborated with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the financial services industry as a whole. During the year, we published an application practice guide and two "Regtech Use Case Booklets" (English version), elaborating on technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments and for greenwashing risk management. We also held the third "FiNETech", bringing together more than 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration. The HKMA is keenly aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risks analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing surveillance work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing surveillance of financial stability risks, and has incorporated analysis of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, which assist central banks and supervisors in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth version of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessment. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participated in analysing the interaction between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the "Practical Guide for Banks to Adopt Green Technologies" (English version), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technologies to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change on the financial industry and the economy as a whole. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in withstanding monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on the direction of foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial industry in the transition to a low-carbon economy. The findings of the above research not only deepened our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, which help to inform the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, this research helps strengthen the HKMA's ongoing surveillance and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings were also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels such as international forums and the "HKMA Research Memorandum". The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (the Research Centre), which is responsible for research work under the Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission enterprises can reap significant benefits from carbon pricing, and highlights its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission enterprises. The study was included in the Research Centre's "Insights from Monetary Research" and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a secured standby liquidity facilities arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into its assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such engagement, we help promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draw lessons from it to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA's "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (Action Agenda), the HKMA is dedicated to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and beyond, supporting technological innovation in the green segment of financial markets, enhancing sustainability disclosures across the industry, expanding the local pool of green talent, and addressing the sustainable finance knowledge gap in Hong Kong and the region. Developing Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform for the region and beyond; catalysing sustainable finance innovation; supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures; and filling the talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region. To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds equivalent to approximately US$28 billion in total, sold to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to more than 110 Government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the programme's impact and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the programme's scope was expanded to cover sustainable projects and renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" (Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report", detailing the allocation of green bond proceeds and the expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing institutional green bonds equivalent to approximately US$3 billion under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This tri-currency issuance covered bonds of different tenors denominated in renminbi, US dollar, and euro. These bonds attracted the participation of a diverse range of investors and received an enthusiastic subscription response, recording subscriptions of over US$15 billion equivalent. Among them, the 20- and 30-year renminbi green bonds were the Government's inaugural issuance and the longest-tenor renminbi bonds issued by the Government to date, providing a new benchmark for the market and further enhancing the demonstrative effect of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the choice of CNH investment products in Hong Kong. In addition, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the green bonds issued by the Government reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers in the region to raise sustainable development funds through Hong Kong's financing platform, the HKMA continued to implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" launched in May 2021, providing subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been widely welcomed by the industry, and as at the end of 2024, it had granted subsidies for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, totalling over US$140 billion. The scheme was extended for three years to 2027 in May 2024, with its scope expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to use Hong Kong's transition financing platform to progressively reduce carbon emissions. - Granted subsidies for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, totalling over US$140 billion (as at the end of 2024) - Extended for three years to 2027, with the scope expanded to cover transition financing instruments. Meanwhile, the HKMA has actively promoted Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, and these efforts have achieved encouraging results. Among them, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government issued offshore local Government Bond in Hong Kong for the fourth time in August, with a total value of RMB7 billion, comprising RMB2.7 billion green bonds, RMB1 billion sustainable bonds, and RMB0.9 billion social responsibility bonds. In September, the People’s Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, with a total value of RMB5 billion, including RMB1.5 billion green bonds. In October, the People’s Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, with a total value of RMB3 billion, comprising RMB1 billion blue bonds and RMB1 billion sustainable bonds. The above issuance activities once again highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable fund flows between the Mainland and around the world. With the above measures, Hong Kong has been able to consolidate its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, in 2024 Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub in Asia for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds, with the total amount of relevant bonds arranged through Hong Kong reaching US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two batches of landmark tokenised green bond in 2023 and 2024, being the world's first tokenised government green bond and the world's first multi-currency digital bond, respectively. These issuances demonstrate the Government's support for market participants in the region in applying asset tokenisation and innovative technology in the green and sustainable finance space. The HKMA also launched the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" in November to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bond, thereby encouraging and supporting the innovative development of Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market. The working group on sustainability disclosures under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) has been working on Hong Kong's adoption of the "IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards" (ISSB Standards). In December 2024, the Government released the "Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong", providing a clear pathway for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to provide support for entities at different stages of readiness to achieve high-quality sustainability disclosures, making sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. It is worth mentioning that we continue to encourage the use of the "Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies" (Questionnaire), which the Steering Group launched in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainability disclosures by enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024, enabling enterprises to complete and submit it online (see the QR code below). The HKMA is enhancing the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, with specific measures including selecting the core questions in the Questionnaire and providing common use scenarios for the Questionnaire. In addition, we also strive to enhance the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information about the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The HKMA leads by example by making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its "Sustainability Report" in accordance with the latest global standards, in order to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains rich content, including the HKMA's climate-related operational risks (climate risk), as well as its plans and implementation progress for achieving climate targets. For details of the sustainability disclosures relating to our own operations, please refer to the chapter "A Sustainable HKMA". Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, and in order to fill the knowledge and talent gaps, the HKMA is strengthening its skills training efforts in the banking sector, as well as promoting knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA, together with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the Foundation level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners" in July 2023. The module aims to help banking industry professionals acquire knowledge and develop relevant professional capabilities in green and sustainable finance in a more effective manner, and covers four key areas of work: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainability/climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainability strategy, compliance, and control. In addition, the Professional level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, targeting middle- and senior-level banking practitioners responsible for relevant work, was also launched in November. To provide the necessary training for banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the administering body of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the Foundation level training programme for the module in May. Following the launch of the Professional level in November, the HKMA will work with the banking sector in 2025 to develop the Professional level training programme. To understand the further skills and training needs of the banking sector, the HKMA is currently working with the banking sector to conduct a study on "Future Banking Talent 2026 to 2030", with the aim of publishing the results of the study in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the "Future Banking Talent 2021 to 2025" document published in June 2020. The results of the follow-up study will provide important reference for the industry, helping it to formulate and adjust its talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. The HKMA has also, through its collaboration with the Steering Group, continued to assist in implementing the Government-funded "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme", which subsidises practitioners, graduates, and students to receive sustainable finance-related training. As at December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses had been registered as eligible training courses under the scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the "2025-26 Budget" that the scheme would be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international collaboration. As a founding member of the "Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment" (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions focusing on the global sustainable finance market, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. In addition, the HKMA supported the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero" (GFANZ) in establishing a chapter in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen skills training efforts in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can complement each other, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritising sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "Capital Preservation first, then Long-term Growth", believing that fully taking into account environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps to reduce relevant investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a firm signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment work. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and striving for more favourable risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment tools to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document available to its investment partners through the annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We partner with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry practice standards, and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and the central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future in which finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), setting out the goal of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "Investment Portfolio" by 2050, as well as mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, further reinforcing its commitment to investing in a sustainable future.  The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practise responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors the relevant implementation through the regular meeting reports of the Sustainable Investing Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As illustrated in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions discussed and the progress of work at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and joined by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures of the HKMA's various functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG goals.  The Sustainable Investing Team works closely with different teams of the Exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors, and assists the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the ESG—particularly climate-related—risks and opportunities across various investments: - Public market investments – The Credit, Regulation and Surveillance Committee, comprising the senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the situation following the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the views of the Sustainable Investing Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Compliance Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investing Team also participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring processes of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (for details, please refer to the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under the "Risk Management" section on page 39). - Private market investments – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams on each investment recommendation.  The HKMA understands that the physical and transition risks brought about by climate change, as well as the related opportunities, will affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund's investments. The "Emissions Gap Report 2024" published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that, unless there is a large-scale global mobilisation to rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties in policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may intensify transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuation. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amid these challenges, as governments and industries shift towards sustainable solutions, this also creates potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG factors.  The HKMA has set the goal of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "Investment Portfolio" by 2050, and continues to advance its work towards this goal through an orderly three-pronged approach (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the "Action Agenda", which reinforced the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA prefers to proactively engage rather than to exclude or divest from investable assets.  Investing in a sustainable future Achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 - Actively expanding the scope and types of sustainable investments, particularly climate transition-themed investments in the public and private markets - Integrating ESG factors into every investment decision, with particular attention to climate change and transition-outlook considerations - Establishing clear ESG expectations that are aligned with international standards and best practices, and requiring all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to comply - Committing to reduce the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from the 2017 level by 2030  Supporting regional transition through investment - Continuing to engage with external investment managers to optimise investment opportunities that drive transition - Continuing to identify and prioritise quality investment opportunities that facilitate Asia's transition and bring positive impact to the world  First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objective. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, with potential impact on investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA is able to seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and that possess advanced technology and good corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not help resolve the carbon emissions problem. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries through the deployment of strategic capital and the active exercise of asset ownership, driving their transition to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about favourable change both for themselves and for the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, in order to drive comprehensive decarbonisation across the entire economy.  As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio depends not only on adjustments to the portfolio itself, but also on a broad economic transition. Although there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategies in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diverse approach to drive transition while supporting the net-zero goals of the Exchange Fund and the world. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilting, and thematic investments targeting various assets aligned with net-zero emission pathways. In the public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, coupled with stewardship to drive corporate transition. In the private markets, there may be a greater focus on transition-enabling investments. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that facilitate climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio.  Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund "Investment Portfolio", with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public market investments – The HKMA launched an actively managed global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of the customised low-carbon equity index to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide funding for sustainable projects while offering competitive returns (for the relevant case study, see the section "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds"). - Private market investments – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capturing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. The HKMA also leverages its extensive network and expertise to actively identify and review investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through establishing strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (for relevant examples, see the section "Working Together to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Beyond").  - Passive investment portfolios that use ESG indices as investment benchmarks - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative investment portfolios that are benchmarked against non-ESG indices - Actively managed investment portfolios with a governance theme - Actively managed ESG investment portfolios with sustainability and climate transition themes - Projects with sustainable features, such as renewable energy infrastructure, as well as green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed on energy transition and decarbonisation in the global, Asian and Global South regions - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation, with a focus on investing in sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" programme, providing Paris Agreement-aligned climate-related investments in emerging markets  The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a quasi-governmental institution.
