The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the key priorities in fulfilling this commitment in 2024 was the plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of the original target, in line with the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan". In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering staff training and physical and mental well-being, as well as striving to advance financial inclusion and enhance the public's financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for the various corporate sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 the HKMA's new target of achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations by 2030, as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"). At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) provides guidance on the implementation of sustainability initiatives relating to corporate operations, staff physical and mental well-being, and community engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, communicating and reporting on corporate sustainability initiatives. The Green Office Focus Group and the Volunteer Service Group, comprising staff from various operating departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former is a platform for brainstorming and proposing ideas on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of staff participation in volunteering activities. In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: environmental, staff and social responsibility.  - Focusing on decarbonisation and digitalisation of the HKMA's day-to-day operations, with a target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 - Adopting green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promoting more environmentally friendly practices to the financial industry and the wider community - Building a proactive workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives - Creating a working environment that promotes collaboration, care and inclusion, values diversity and strengthens staff's sense of belonging - Providing a quality working environment and promoting a healthy lifestyle - Cultivating a culture of caring for society - Incorporating social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management - Advancing financial inclusion and enhancing the public's financial literacy through consumer education activities  The HKMA is concerned about climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its own corporate operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of its original commitment, as part of the "Action Plan". The HKMA has revised its roadmap for the transition towards net zero, with a focus on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its day-to-day operations, concentrating on reducing carbon emissions, saving energy and paper, and recycling waste, while making full use of the improvements made by local power companies in their fuel mix for electricity generation. In addition, the HKMA has established a digitalised working environment to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, the HKMA recognises the importance of cultivating a culture of sustainability, and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under the overriding 2030 net-zero emissions target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and adopting low-carbon procurement wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offsetting programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting programmes to cover all remaining major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its actual operations, the HKMA continues to promote the low-carbon transition of the market, ranging from the introduction of electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and collecting coins for recirculation in the market. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as promoting staff physical and mental well-being and caring for society.  Under the HKMA's overall corporate risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing the potential risks and threats, including those arising from climate change, that the HKMA faces in its day-to-day operations. To more effectively assess the possible impact of climate change on its operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the HKMA's office design incorporates a number of measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fire and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans to incorporate comprehensive measures covering not only its offices but also its communication and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to carry out contingency measures. The HKMA has also been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking the greenhouse gas emissions generated by its own operations, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions related to its corporate operations by 2030. These targets have been set with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology. The HKMA uses the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report its corporate emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's main greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions arising from the consumption of fossil fuels for electricity generation. As data from individual suppliers is not available, the HKMA takes a conservative approach in estimating Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfill and staff air travel and commuting. The detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and basis of the agency's verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" attached at the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, upholding the same climate-related standards that it expects of the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees.  As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024, and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve full green mobility. The HKMA continues to incorporate environmental considerations into the design, operation and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in the various renovation works in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and renovation materials or traded in old items for discounts on new purchases, thereby reducing waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews the energy consumption and energy-saving measures of its offices and data centre, and in its 2024 data centre facility upgrade project adopted a modular-design uninterruptible power supply system, further optimising the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operating efficiency at partial loads, and features advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. Through its digital workplace, the HKMA has strengthened internal virtual collaboration, which, coupled with streamlined workflows, has effectively reduced paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the service life of its mobile and desktop devices with reference to manufacturers' software update cycles, which can prolong the secure usage period of the devices. To reduce waste generated in its offices, the HKMA follows the "4R" principles, namely refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has set up recycling bins at various convenient locations in its offices to recycle different materials. To increase the recycling rate, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit net bags in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending the food waste it collects to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Waste Reduction Pledge for Events", committing to take measures to reduce waste generated by its various events. The HKMA continues to give priority to procuring goods that meet the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to carefully plan their trips, for example by combining multiple journeys as far as possible when attending overseas events. At the corporate level, the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing its annual air travel carbon emissions by about 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in a Gold Standard-certified carbon offsetting programme to offset the remaining air travel carbon emissions; the programme focuses on renewable energy generation and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged a number of learning activities for staff, such as talks and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on 22 April 2024 through the whole of May, the HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month", themed "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This was a good opportunity to promote the HKMA's commitment and drive towards environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The activities included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" to encourage staff to practise green living, a "Save the Earth" quiz game, and a "Kokedama" indoor plant care workshop originating from Japan; the results of the waste audit were also shared, and best practices in recycling were introduced by a community recycling centre operator. To sustain the momentum of the "Green Month", the HKMA launched a recycling campaign in October lasting about six months, highlighting the responsible handling of waste and reminding staff that small changes in individual habits, when brought together, can significantly enhance the overall recycling performance of the organisation. One of the highlights of the campaign was the launch of the "Green Tips in Action" video, in which several senior management members shared recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screen savers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles and electronic reminders to remind staff to take action to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff questionnaire survey to understand their awareness of sustainability and to collect their views on the proposed green office measures. The survey results will help formulate future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the environmental data ("the Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel for the year 2024, together with their respective intensities. In addition, the Data includes Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions arising from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for the years 2023 and 2024, together with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data was compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, comprising 5 offices located at (1) Two International Finance Centre, (2) Hopewell Centre, (3) One Pacific Place, (4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and (5) International Commerce Centre, and 1 warehouse located at (6) Roxy Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance of the accuracy and reliability of the Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the 6 assets. This verification work was carried out in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to enable us to form an opinion and reach a conclusion so as to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducted reliability testing. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work was conducted with complete independence and impartiality. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - the Data is substantially accurate and reliable; - the HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025
